author: Michael Larabel
description: AMD GAIA 0.25 is out this week as the latest feature release for this open-source project that began as "Generative AI Is Awesome" and is now going on a tag line of "AMD's open-source agent factory" in building/using local AI agents on AMD Ryzen AI hardware...
title: AMD GAIA 0.25 Brings Several Improvements For Local AI Agents On Ryzen AI

author: Michael Larabel
description: In addition to introducing the new Intel BFF driver, the Error Detection And Correction "EDAC" kernel subsystem is sunsetting a number of old hardware drivers due to increased noise to AI/LLM-generated bug fixes for these likely unused or minimally used drivers...
title: Linux 7.4 Sunsetting Old EDAC Drivers Due To "AI Generated Fixes Frenzy"

author: Michael Larabel
description: With Linux 7.3 there are some nice Btrfs performance improvements to enjoy while the in-development Linux 7.4 kernel is set to bring some additional performance optimizations for this copy-on-write file-system...
title: Btrfs Brings More Performance Improvements For Linux 7.4

author: Michael Larabel
description: An Intel engineer opened the pull requests today for adding Intel XeSS support to Valve's Proton for Steam Play along with associated changes to VKD3D-Proton and DXVK...
title: Intel Working To Add XMX-Accelerated XeSS To Valve's Steam Play (Proton)

author: Michael Larabel
description: Last week I wrote about Linus Torvalds leveraging AI to come up with a hefty Linux kernel improvement using Claude Code. The code is for reading from the page cache without folio references to help workloads of small reads from a single file across many CPU threads. Meta engineer Kiryl Shutsemau has taken that code and reworked it and showing extremely promising performance results...
title: Linus Torvalds' AI Code Improved: Huge Performance Wins With Reworked Code

author: Michael Larabel
description: The Motorola 68000 "m68k" CPU support continues being maintained in the mainline Linux kernel and continuing to see new hardware support for these vintage systems from the likes of Commodore Amiga, Atari, and early Apple Macintosh models...
title: Linux In 2026 Continues Improving Support For Benefiting Old Atari & Amiga Hardware

author: Michael Larabel
description: Canonical's Multipass software is used for orchestrating Ubuntu virtual instances with a single command to launch Ubuntu VMs across Windows, macOS, and Linux. Multipass 1.17 was released today and they are now offering direct support for enabling non-Ubuntu Linux distributions as well...
title: Canonical's Multipass 1.17 Adds Direct Support For Non-Ubuntu Linux Distros

author: Michael Larabel
description: GNU Linux-libre 7.3 is now available following yesterday's Linux 7.3 release. The GNU Linux-libre downstream continues stripping out driver/hardware support where dependent upon firmware blobs or other proprietary elements deemed out of line with free software ideals...
title: GNU Linux-libre 7.3-gnu Removes More Firmware Blobs

author: Michael Larabel
description: Stemming from a bug report one month ago with GNOME 51 over high GPU usage while the monitor is sleeping, a set of 17 patches were merged today for addressing this issue...
title: GNOME Mutter Lands Improvement For Reducing GPU Work While In Power Savings Mode

author: Michael Larabel
description: Following the interesting SpacemiT K3 RVA23 RISC-V SoC, SpacemiT today announced the V100 server-class RISC-V processor...
title: SpacemiT Announces The V100 Server-Class RISC-V Processor

author: Michael Larabel
description: There is yet-another-Linux-file-system attempt... An initial request for comments (RFC) patch series was sent out this morning for BeamFS. The proposed BeamFS is a Reed-Solomon protected file-system...
title: BeamFS Sent Out As Newest File-System Proposal For Linux

author: Michael Larabel
description: The ARM64 code for Linux 7.4 is stripping away its support for big-endian kernel builds for 64-bit ARM...
title: Linux 7.4 Removing Its Broken & Rarely Touched Code For ARM64 Big Endian

author: Michael Larabel
description: Going back to July 2025 the open-source Radeon RADV Vulkan driver has offered experimental host image copy support with the API's VK_EXT_host_image_copy extension. This has been for RDNA1 and newer GPUs while now GFX10 RDNA 1 GPUs have this extension enabled by default while also enabling experimental support for prior GFX9 era GPUs too...
title: RADV Promotes VK_EXT_host_image_copy To Enabled By Default For RDNA1 GPUs

author: Michael Larabel
description: Among the early pull requests sent out in advance of the Linux 7.4 kernel merge window opening were the driver core updates. Standing out here is the new TAINT_FORCED_BIND for dealing with the recent major fuzzing "attack" by AI agents/bots testing impractical driver/hardware combinations...
title: TAINT_FORCED_BIND Sent In For Linux 7.4 To Deal With Major Fuzzing Attack
